title: Dordt British: external and internal preparatories
source_text: L. Quae sint autem illae dispositiones, explicat postea verbis Theologorum Britan-norum qui Synodo Dordracenae interfuerunt. Qui sic loquuntur in judicio suo ad Art. 3. & 4. Sunt quaedam opera externa, ab hominibus ordinarie requisita, priusquam ad statum regenerationis, aut conversionis perducantur, &c. Sunt etiam quaedam ef-fecta interna ad conversionem, sive regenerationem praevia, quae virtute Verbi, Spiri-tusque, in nondum justificatorum cordibus excitantur. Qualia sunt, notitia voluntatis divinae, sensus peccati, timor poenae, cogitatio de liberatione, spes aliqua veniae. Quibus postea subjungunt, Nam sicut in generatione hominis naturali, multae sunt praeviae dispo-sitiones, quae formae inductionem praecedunt, ita & in Spirituali, per multas anteceda-neas gratiae actiones, ad Spiritualem nativitatem pervenitur.
pass_a_gloss: But what those dispositions are he afterward explains in the words of the British theologians who took part in the Synod of Dort. Who thus speak in their judgment on Articles 3 and 4: There are certain external works ordinarily required of men before they are brought to the state of regeneration or conversion, etc. There are also certain internal effects prior to conversion or regeneration, which by the power of the Word and Spirit are excited in the hearts of those not yet justified. Such are knowledge of the divine will, sense of sin, fear of punishment, thought of deliverance, some hope of pardon. To which they afterward add: For as in the natural generation of man there are many prior dispositions which precede the induction of the form, so also in the spiritual, through many antecedent actions of grace one arrives at spiritual birth.
pass_b_english: British at Dort: some external works ordinarily required before regeneration; also internal effects—knowledge of God's will, sense of sin, fear, hope of pardon.
As natural generation has prior dispositions, so spiritual birth follows many antecedent grace-acts.

choices.why: Key lemma for De Justitia densify §1084.
